c.tagline: Cobblestones, kalesa bells, and candlelight over Calle Crisologo

card: Cards are accepted at larger hotels and a few upscale restaurants in the heritage core, but most tricycles, kalesa rides, small eateries, and the public market are cash-only. ATMs (BDO, Landbank, Metrobank) cluster around Plaza Salcedo and downtown.

taxi.color: No standardized color scheme — tricycles are independently owned and painted
taxi.fare: ₱15-20 minimum tricycle fare; ₱150-300 for a 30-45 minute kalesa heritage-district tour
taxi.fareNote: Agree on the kalesa fare before boarding — rates are per carriage (up to 3-4 people), not per person; tricycles are unmetered, so confirm price for longer trips

emergency.medical: Gabriela Silang General Hospital (city-run) and Metro Vigan Community Hospital are the two main hospitals serving Vigan
emergency.note: Serious trauma cases are sometimes referred to larger facilities in Laoag or San Fernando; travel insurance is recommended

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Very walkable — the UNESCO heritage core around Calle Crisologo and Plaza Salcedo is compact, flat, and pedestrian-friendly (parts of Calle Crisologo close to vehicles in the evening). Most major sights are within a 15-20 minute walk of each other.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers, including women — Vigan is a small, tourism-oriented heritage city with a strong local police and tourism-police presence around Calle Crisologo and Plaza Salcedo, especially in the evenings.
safety.crime: Petty crime is low; standard precautions apply (watch belongings in the public market, use licensed tricycles at night, agree fares upfront).

hood_landmark.Plaza Salcedo / Downtown Poblacion: Plaza Salcedo dancing fountain and Vigan Cathedral

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed heart of Vigan — ancestral Spanish-Chinese mestizo houses, antique shops, and horse-drawn kalesa clattering over cobblestones.
Vigan's civic and religious core, anchored by the baroque cathedral, the archbishop's palace, and the nightly light-and-water show at Plaza Salcedo.
A working artisan quarter where centuries-old burnay pottery is still hand-thrown and fired in wood-burning kilns.
A quiet hilltop across the Mestizo River famous for its historic bell tower with sweeping views over Vigan and the surrounding rice fields.
The coastal fringe near the airport and Long Beach, offering a low-key seaside break from the heritage-district crowds.

water.note: Stick to bottled or filtered water, as most locals do.

transit.sys: No formal public transit system — tricycles, kalesa, and jeepneys handle local movement; multicabs run longer routes to nearby towns
transit.hours: Roughly 5am-10pm; kalesa mainly operate daytime through early evening
transit.map: No official transit map — routes are informal; ask hotel staff for jeepney routes to outlying barangays
transit.note: Calle Crisologo restricts motor vehicles in the evening, becoming a pedestrian and kalesa-only heritage walk

transport.air: Laoag International Airport (LAO), about 85 km / 1.5-2 hours north, is the main gateway with Cebu Pacific and PAL Express flights from Manila; a small local Vigan Airport has limited regional service
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Vigan or the region
transport.bus: Partas, Farinas Trans, and Dominion operate direct overnight/day buses from Manila to Vigan, roughly 8-9 hours
transport.ferry: No direct passenger ferry service to Vigan
transport.car: Drive via NLEX to TPLEX to the MacArthur Highway/Ilocos coastal roads from Manila, roughly 7-8 hours

airport.name: Laoag International Airport
airport.distance: ~85 km / 1.5-2 hour drive north of Vigan
airport.transport: Van/shuttle transfers, private car hire, or bus connections from Laoag city to Vigan

net.m: Good coverage in Vigan from both national carriers
net.w: Most cafes, restaurants near Calle Crisologo, and hotels offer free wifi
net.ops: Globe Telecom, Smart Communications (including TNT/TM prepaid sub-brands)
net.fwn: Free wifi common at cafes and hotels near the heritage core
net.ap: Prepaid SIMs widely available from local shops

tip.s: Tipping is not mandatory but appreciated — round up or leave 5-10% at restaurants without an existing service charge
tip.r: For kalesa drivers and tricycle rides, a small tip (₱10-20) for good service is a nice gesture, not expected
